takeaway: A dry, sunny, gusty Sunday. Costa Rica's weather service (IMN) has few clouds and strong morning trade-wind gusts on the North Pacific today, with no rain in the forecast here; the showers stay on the Central and South Pacific. Nicoya should reach about 34°C. For surf, it's offshore every day through at least Thursday, with 4–6 feet at 13–14 seconds today and Monday and a new long-period pulse (15–16 seconds) from Tuesday night into Thursday. The rest of October looks mostly dry. The models still show a wetter stretch around Nov 2–6, a bit stronger today and centered near Nov 4, while IMN still expects the dry season to settle in. No tropical threat to Costa Rica, and the prolonged-rain watch stays low.

periods.label: Days 1–3 (Sun–Tue, Oct 25–27)
periods.pattern: IMN's Sunday forecast for the North Pacific is few clouds with occasional gusts through the early morning and morning, partly to mostly clear with moderate winds in the afternoon, and partly cloudy tonight. Nicoya's high is about 34°C with a low around 22°C. IMN says morning trade gusts run 30–50 km/h around the country and up to 70 km/h on the North Pacific, with little rain. The model averages agree: only about 1–4 mm (under 0.2 inch) a day near Nosara today through Tuesday. The marine forecast still has scattered showers and a few storms well offshore.
periods.implications: Good outdoor days. Expect hot, sunny, windy mornings that calm a bit in the afternoon. A stray shower is possible but unlikely to matter. Secure anything light on the beach in the morning gusts.

periods.label: Days 4–7 (Wed–Sat, Oct 28–31)
periods.pattern: All models keep a northeast-to-east breeze over Nicaragua and northern Costa Rica, lighter around Tuesday night and Wednesday and firmer again Thursday. Rain near Nosara stays light, about 1–3 mm a day, with a little more Saturday (2–4 mm). The AI-based European average shows a weak dip in pressure near the Nicoya coast around Friday evening, but it brings almost no rain with it. IMN's weekly outlook (Oct 22–28) describes the shift to the dry season: morning trade gusts of 40–60 km/h that ease in the afternoon, a chance of isolated afternoon storms, and isolated night showers on the Pacific coast.
periods.implications: Mostly dry, sunny, and breezy. Good for outdoor plans. A passing evening or night shower is possible, especially by Saturday.
periods.confidence: High on mostly dry through Friday. Moderate for Saturday.

periods.label: Days 8–15 (Sun Nov 1 – Sun Nov 8)
periods.pattern: The trades keep blowing over Nicaragua in every model, but the band of tropical showers south of Costa Rica pushes north over the Nicoya coast in early November. Near Nosara, the averages show about 6 mm on Nov 2 and a peak around Nov 4: roughly 11 mm (0.4 inch) in the American average, 16 mm in the AI-based European average, and about 20–25 mm (close to an inch) in the European average. Showers ease to about 5–10 mm a day by Nov 6–7. The regular American run is similarly wet around Nov 4 and shows a weak low just off the Gulf of Nicoya around Nov 1; the regular European run is lighter, under 10 mm a day. IMN's long-range outlook (Oct 26–Nov 22) still calls for drier-than-normal weather, with the dry season taking hold on the North and Central Pacific in the first week of November.
periods.implications: Late October looks good. Keep plans for roughly Nov 2–6 flexible, with Nov 4 the most likely wet day. Think of it as a few showery or stormy days, not a washout, though IMN and the models disagree.
periods.confidence: Moderate-high on a dry end to October. Low to moderate on early November.

surfWinds.regime: Caribbean trades, offshore at Nosara, every day through at least Thursday. Breezy offshore today, lighter Tuesday night and Wednesday, then a little firmer Thursday.
surfWinds.detail: The Papagayo marine forecast (issued 1:05 a.m. PDT Sunday, 2:05 a.m. Costa Rica time) has northeast to east winds around 20 knots in the Gulf of Papagayo this morning, easing to 10–15 knots this afternoon, and northeast to east 10–15 elsewhere, which is offshore here. Tonight the gulf freshens to 15–20 with northeast 10 elsewhere. Monday is northeast 10–15, Tuesday northeast 10, Tuesday night nearly calm in the gulf, Wednesday northeast 10, and Thursday northeast to east 10–15. Good news for Monday: the westerly winds just south of the peninsula are now forecast at about 10–15 knots tonight and around 10 knots Monday, weaker than yesterday's forecast, so the risk of Monday afternoon turning side-on or onshore is lower. Swell: 4–6 feet at 14 seconds today, 13 seconds tonight (west swell) and Monday, 11 seconds Monday night (west-northwest), 3–5 feet at 13 seconds Tuesday, then 3–5 feet at 15–16 seconds from Tuesday night through Thursday. Nicaragua: every model keeps easterly trades over Nicaragua into early November, so Nicaragua should be offshore all day most days. That's a good sign for clean Nosara mornings, but it doesn't mean Nosara stays offshore all day.
surfWinds.bestWindows: Today and Monday mornings: offshore with 4–6 feet at 13–14 seconds. Go early, before the afternoon sea breeze. Wednesday and Thursday mornings: light offshore with the new 15–16-second pulse, so sets come bigger and less often than the average height suggests. Tuesday is the smallest, shortest-period day.
surfWinds.confidence: High on offshore mornings through Thursday. Moderate on how late into each afternoon it holds. Moderate on the size of the long-period pulse.

gyreWatch.status: Watch only, low. Nothing established and nothing building in the next week. The early-November wet signal is a little stronger today, but it still doesn't look like a multi-day soaking setup.
gyreWatch.possibleTiming: Around Nov 2–6, most likely near Nov 4.
gyreWatch.supporting: All three model averages bring the shower band north over the Nicoya coast in early November, and they all got a bit wetter near Nosara around Nov 4. The regular American run and the AI-based European average both show weak areas of low pressure near the Gulf of Nicoya (around Oct 30–Nov 1), and the American run keeps a loose spin offshore to the south around Nov 6.
gyreWatch.conflicting: No model average shows a broad, slow-spinning low parked off Costa Rica, and all keep northeast-to-east trades over Nicaragua and northern Costa Rica into early November. A multi-day soak usually needs days of steady wind off the Pacific, which is the opposite. The regular European run stays fairly light. IMN's long-range outlook calls for drier-than-normal weather through Nov 22, and NOAA's tropics outlook expects East Pacific storm activity to wane in November. Hurricane Vance is far off southern Mexico, and the U.S. hurricane center expects no new storms in the Caribbean or near Central America in the next week.

whatChanged: IMN dropped the afternoon showers on the peninsula: today is just few clouds and gusty, after yesterday's call for scattered showers. The westerly winds just south of the peninsula tonight and Monday were downgraded, so Monday afternoon looks cleaner, and Monday's swell is now 13 seconds instead of 11. The long-period pulse now runs from Tuesday night through Thursday. The early-November wet signal got a little stronger and more focused on Nov 4, especially in the European average, and two models now show weak lows near the Gulf of Nicoya. IMN's weekly and long-range outlooks are unchanged.
practical: Today through Tuesday: sunny, hot, and windy, with offshore surf mornings today and Monday. Wednesday and Thursday: catch the new long-period swell in light offshore wind, and watch for stronger rip currents. Late October stays mostly dry. Keep Nov 2–6 plans flexible, especially around Nov 4. No tropical storm threat to Costa Rica.
